note: T3-16 item 7 (docs/specs/T3-16.md, "The path rule"): request paths the native request and the core's reference transport refuse before anything is sent, and paths they accept. A refused path holds a . or .. segment as written or percent-encoded, a backslash, a control character, or an escape that does not decode to UTF-8. Read by modules/session/android/src/test/java/dev/octave/session/http/RequestPathTest.kt and packages/core/src/adapters/request-path.test.ts. An accepted path reaches the server as the session's base path plus the path, byte for byte. The vectors with a `why` were added for spec-check note 5, where the Kotlin and TypeScript decoders can disagree; the result each records is the one both sides must give. So a path is also refused when a % does not begin two hex digits or the escapes do not decode to UTF-8, a rule beyond P1 to P4 that neither C1 nor a lenient decoder supplies. Paths OkHttp would re-encode (a raw space or a raw non-ASCII character) are not here: Kotlin refuses them by C1 and the reference transport has no C1 (RequestPathTest holds the Kotlin half).

refused.name: lone percent
refused.why: a malformed escape: OkHttp 5.5.1 sends it unchanged (recorded at the freeze), decodeURIComponent throws, and a server may read it either way; refused on both sides

refused.name: short escape
refused.why: a malformed escape: OkHttp 5.5.1 sends it unchanged (recorded at the freeze), decodeURIComponent throws; refused on both sides

refused.name: non-hex escape
refused.why: a malformed escape: OkHttp 5.5.1 sends it unchanged (recorded at the freeze), decodeURIComponent throws; refused on both sides

refused.name: overlong UTF-8 dot-dot
refused.why: the overlong form of .. (0xC0 0xAE) is not UTF-8: OkHttp 5.5.1 sends it unchanged, decodeURIComponent throws, and a lenient decoder on a server or proxy may read it as a dot; encodeURIComponent never writes it

refused.name: semicolon after a dot-dot

noteT3_24: T3-24 item 5 (docs/specs/T3-24.md, "The vectors"): the vectors with a why that starts T3-24 were appended by the T3-24 Tests step. A path is also refused when any round of up to four percent-decodings holds a ; (P6) or a control character (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F; P3), a segment made only of dots and the nine dot-like characters with at least one dot-like (P4), or an escape run that is not UTF-8 (P5), and when the fourth decoding still holds an escape (P7). In rounds 1 to 4 a % that begins no escape is a literal. Both readers take only refused and accepted.
